# Disagreement Log — T12_002 (Testament of Simeon)
**Chapter:** T12_002 | **Verses:** 7 sections (~17 verses)
**Translators compared:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA | **Arbiter:** SOPHIA

| # | Verse | Issue | EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA | SOPHIA ruling |
|---|-------|-------|------|-------|--------|---------------|
| 1 | 2:2 | Spirit title | "prince-of-deceit" (hyphenated) | "prince of error" | "prince of deceit" | "prince of error" — LOGOS; "error" better reflects Greek planē |
| 2 | 3:3 | Illness cause | "I was weakened in my limbs for two years" | "I afflicted my soul, and was weakened in my limbs" | "The Lord weakened my hands and feet for two years" | Combined: "LORD weakened my hands and feet" — passive divine agency preserved |
| 3 | 4:2 | Judah's character | "Judah our father the LORD gave understanding" | "our father Judah" | "our brother Judah" | "Judah our brother" — PNEUMA correct; Judah is Simeon's brother, not father |
| 4 | 5:1 | Messiah description | "God-and-man" (bracketed) | "God and man, He shall save all the Gentiles" | "God and man together — who will save all humanity" | "God and man; he shall save all the nations and the race of Israel" — explicit dual scope |
| 5 | 6:1–4 | Joseph section placement | Before priestly blessing (ch 5) | After priestly blessing | After priestly blessing | LOGOS/PNEUMA order retained — Joseph as exemplar follows the theological climax |

---
*SOPHIA notes: Testament of Simeon's central theme is jealousy as a demonic spirit. All three translators render the core narrative well. The "prince of error/deceit" title matters because Greek planē (wandering/error) is theologically distinct from Latin "deceit." SOPHIA adopts LOGOS's "error." The Judah reference is a scribal-confusion point — Judah is brother, not father.*
